our_title: Sq twins now disagree: bdgraph fails on partial sequential failure, vdgraph tolerates it
ran: Pristine 7.0.18 bipartfi scan (q{strat=f}, np=3, allocation failing on rank 1 inside bgraphBipartGg/Fm, nth=6,15,16): '(0),(1),(2): ERROR: bdgraphBipartSq: internal error', ret=1 on all ranks, although ranks 0 and 2 hold valid partitions. vdgraphSeparateSq has no such test any more (5b43f6d2), so the same event in ordering is tolerated (best separator of the succeeding processes is used).
read_only: vdgraph side read: vdgraph_separate_sq.c:177-190 (no partial-failure test after the reduction; the operator :91-110 skips failed processes).
evidence: bdgraph_bipart_sq.c:213 'if ((reduglbtab[4] != 0) && (reduglbtab[4] != dgrfptr->s.procglbnbr)) { errorPrint ("bdgraphBipartSq: internal error");' versus 5b43f6d2 removing from vdgraph_separate_sq.c the '#ifdef SCOTCH_DEBUG_VDGRAPH2 ... (reduloctab[3] != dgrfptr->s.procglbnbr)) { errorPrint ("vdgraphSeparateSq: internal error (1)");' block as 'useless and bogus'.

fix_options.label: A: debug-only partial-failure check in bdgraphBipartSq
fix_options.summary: Same tolerance as the vdgraph twin in release builds; the consistency check stays under SCOTCH_DEBUG_BDGRAPH2.
fix_options.tested: applies on the series; compiles with and without -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL; not run
fix_options.maintainer_fit: matches his own 5b43f6d2 on the twin

fix_options.label: B: keep both as they are
fix_options.summary: Accept that bipartitioning is strict and separation tolerant.

upstream_fix_review.details: Each commit is right for its own file; together they make the twins diverge. Not a crash: a user-visible failure of dgmap/dgpart on one process's transient OOM where dgord would succeed.
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Our 7.0.17 G22 0001 and G23 0011 kept the two twins identical (debug-only count test in both).

our_title: bgraphBipartSt guards its test-result check with the Vgraph debug macro
read_only: src/libscotch/bgraph_bipart_st.c:308-315; found by a whole-tree scan of SCOTCH_DEBUG_<module> macros against file prefixes after aa24a7cb/cc440aca (the only remaining cross-module use in libscotch).
why_not_run: debug-only check; compiles identically under -DSCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL (where both macros are set)
